newsitem.title: USA: Japan trade surplus with U.S. rises in October.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus with U.S. rises in October.

text.p: Japan's politically sensitive trade surplus with the United States surged in October, the first such rise in 20 months, as Japanese carmakers took advantage of the weak yen to export more vehicles, the Finance Ministry said Monday.
But Japan's overall surplus declined year-on-year for the 23rd consecutive month, surprising many economists who had expected it to rise.
The overall trade surplus fell 12.9 percent in October from a year earlier to 470.86 billion yen ($4.24 billion), the 23rd consecutive month it has declined on a year-on-year basis.
Japan's trade surplus with the United States in October rose 31.3 percent from a year earlier to 354.79 billion yen ($3.19 billion), mainly due to a strong rise in automobile exports.
The dollar edged down against the yen on the news as dealers focused on the growing surplus against the United States rather than the decline in the overall trade surplus.

Dealers have speculated that a rise in the trade surplus could prompt the U.S. government to push down the value of the dollar against the yen to redress the trade imbalance, as a strong yen tends to hit Japanese exports.

Economists had expected a mild rise in the overall surplus after data for the first 20 days of October showed the surplus ballooning by more than 20 percent. Exports typically rise toward the end of the month.
The trade surplus fell in October despite strong export growth mainly because oil import costs rose, and economists still believe the overall trade surplus will soon start to rise.
The quantity of oil imports was virtually unchanged from a year earlier, while the value of imports soared 41.6 percent as oil prices rose 38 percent, ministry data showed.

"There is a structural change of trade occurring...in the near future, we will see a so-called 'bottoming out' phenomenon of the trade surplus," said Masaru Takagi, chief economist at Fuji Research Institute. He predicted the surplus would bottom out and then start to climb again.
Takagi said he expects the yen to rise to as high as 105 yen to the dollar in the not-too-distant future.
The yen traded at 111.48 to the dollar in New York at mid-morning.
A Finance Ministry official told reporters he did not think the declining trend in the surplus with the United States had changed despite the big rise in the surplus in October.

Yasushi Okuda, an economist at BZW Securities, attributed the strong rise in exports to the United States as a reaction to the previous year, when auto exports fell dramatically due to the strong yen.
"But as overall export prices of Japanese products have been decreasing, we will see a reasonable year-on-year increase," Okuda said.
